# `Television`

A TV on a CEC bus. With a `Television`, you set the TV's power with `spec.power`, and the TV wakes, switches to the `Player`'s `Display`, and goes to standby with the `Player`'s room. A CEC bus has at most one TV, and the TV is always at physical address `0.0.0.0` and logical address `0`, so `spec.cec.bus` identifies it. A CEC node workload is the pod of the `equipment-operator-cec` `DaemonSet` that runs one adapter of the bus. The command adapter is the first adapter in the `CECBus`'s `spec.adapters` that is in `Control` and has a logical address. Its node workload applies `spec.power` and reads the TV's power for `status.session.powerReadAt`, so the TV gets each command once. A `Display`'s adapter is the first adapter in `spec.adapters` that names that `Display` and is in `Control` with a logical address. Its node workload wakes the TV and puts it in standby for a session on that `Display`, because Active Source carries the sender's physical address, and that adapter announces the `Display`'s physical address. When a `CECBus` in `Control` finds a TV and no `Television` names that bus, the operator creates a `Television` with the bus's name and the label `equipment.liken.sh/discovered`. To set its spec, apply your own `Television` with the bus's name. The object keeps the label, and the operator keeps the object while no other `Television` names the bus. When you create a `Television` with another name for the same bus, the operator deletes the discovered one. The operator manages only a labeled `Television` whose name is the bus's name, so a labeled `Television` with any other name is yours.

## spec

The protocol block and the power state you want. You write every field of the spec, and the operator writes none.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="spec--cec"></span>`cec` | [object](#speccec) | no | Controls the TV over a CEC bus. The command adapter's node workload reads the TV's power and sends it power commands. |
| <span id="spec--power"></span>`power` | string | no | The power state you want for the TV: `On` or `Standby`. When the field is absent, the operator leaves the TV's power alone. Quote `On` in YAML, as `power: "On"`, because kubectl reads a bare `On` as the boolean `true`, and the API server refuses it. The command adapter's node workload applies each `metadata.generation` once, so when a person turns the TV off with its own remote, the operator does not turn it back on. To apply the same value again, change the spec, for example by removing the field and adding it back. A new `Television` applies its `spec.power`, so a GitOps prune or a restore that deletes and creates the object applies it again. When several `Television` objects name one bus, only the one whose `InCharge` condition is `True` applies `spec.power`. When that one is deleted, the next one applies its `spec.power` once, as a new object does. The node workload reads the TV's power first, and sends nothing when the TV already reports the state. A TV reports its old state for a while after a command, so the node workload trusts the read only when it sent the TV no command in the last 15 seconds. For `On` it sends Image View On, which also asks the TV to show the sender's input, so the TV can switch to the adapter's `Display` as it wakes. For `Standby` it sends Standby to the TV alone. Then it reads the power every second. When 10 seconds pass and the TV reports neither the new state nor the change toward it (`ToOn` or `ToStandby`), it sends the command again. It sends at most three commands for one generation, and stops reading after 30 seconds. A new generation cancels the work on an older one. `status.powerGeneration` and the `PowerApplied` condition report the result. One of: `On`, `Standby`. |

### spec.cec

Controls the TV over a CEC bus. The command adapter's node workload reads the TV's power and sends it power commands.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="speccec--bus"></span>`bus` | string | yes | The name of the `CECBus` that the TV is on. The bus must be in `Control` for the operator to read the TV's power or send it commands, because an adapter in `Listen` sends nothing. |

## status

What the bus reports about the TV, and what the operator and the CEC node workloads did.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="status--cec"></span>`cec` | [object](#statuscec) | no | The TV's CEC identity, copied from the TV's entry in the `CECBus`'s `status.devices`. A field is absent until the TV reports it, and some TVs never report every field. For example, a TV can answer power status requests in standby and never answer Give OSD Name. |
| <span id="status--power"></span>`power` | string | no | The power status that the TV last reported: `On`, `Standby`, `ToOn`, or `ToStandby`. The operator never reads the TV's power on a timer, because some TVs switch their own input when they get messages they did not expect. An adapter in `Control` sends Give Device Power Status when it joins the bus, before and after each command it sends the TV, and for each `status.session.powerAsk` on the `Receiver`. Between those reads, the operator updates the value from messages on the bus. A Report Power Status from the TV sets the reported value. A Standby to the TV or to all devices sets `Standby`. A Routing Change, a Set Stream Path, or a Request Active Source from the TV, or an Active Source from any device, sets `On`. An adapter receives only broadcasts and the messages sent to its own address. So when a person turns the TV on or off with the TV's own remote and the TV sends none of those messages, the value is out of date until the next read. A `powerAsk` reads the TV first, so its result does not depend on this value. A TV in deep standby or an eco mode can stop answering. After two reads in a row with no answer, the field is absent and `Reachable` is `False`. After one missed answer, the field keeps the last value, because a TV can miss one answer while it wakes. The operator never reports `Standby` for a TV that did not answer. |
| <span id="status--activesource"></span>`activeSource` | string | no | The physical address in the last Active Source message on the bus. The operator reads it from the first adapter in the `CECBus`'s `spec.adapters` that has a current entry and has received an Active Source. CEC has no message that asks the TV which input it shows, and a TV that switches to its own apps or to an input without CEC sends nothing. So this field can differ from what the TV shows. |
| <span id="status--activedisplay"></span>`activeDisplay` | string | no | The `Display` whose physical address is `activeSource`, which is the machine output that the TV last switched to over CEC. The operator looks first at the `Display` objects that the `CECBus`'s `spec.adapters` name, then at the other `Display` objects on the adapters' machines, and takes the first by name when two match. The field is absent when `activeSource` is absent or when no `Display` has that address, for example when a streaming player or a game console is the active source. Like `activeSource`, it can differ from what the TV shows. |
| <span id="status--powergeneration"></span>`powerGeneration` | integer | no | The last `metadata.generation` whose `spec.power` the command adapter's node workload applied. The node workload applies `spec.power` only when the generation differs from this field, so a restart of the node workload does not apply a generation twice. |
| <span id="status--session"></span>`session` | [object](#statussession) | no | The `Receiver` session whose input shows on this TV, so that the TV wakes and goes to standby with the `Player`. The operator's `Deployment` writes it under its own field manager. So your apply of the spec does not remove it, and a write of it does not change `metadata.generation` or apply `spec.power` again. The operator takes the `Display` that is the monitor of the session's input in the `Receiver`'s `spec.inputs`, and writes the session to the `Television` whose `status.displays` lists that `Display`. It writes a new `wokeAt` when it sees the room wake: a `Play` starts on an existing session, the `Player`'s screen wakes, a `powerAsk` turns the room on, or a session appears with its `Play` or its screen already on. It writes a new `standbyAt` only when a `powerAsk` turns the room off. The `Display`'s adapter then wakes the TV and makes the `Display` the active source, or puts the TV in standby. When the operator starts, it keeps each session that it finds here with the same `Player` and `Display`, with its `awake`, `wokeAt`, and `standbyAt` unchanged, and it wakes nothing and puts nothing in standby. The operator removes the field 60 seconds after the `Receiver`'s session ends, the `Receiver` is deleted, or the `Receiver`'s address changes, unless a session of the same `Player` starts first. So when `media-operator` removes a session and writes it again a moment later, the TV is not woken again. If the API server refuses the removal, the operator tries again after 10 seconds. |
| <span id="status--wokeat"></span>`wokeAt` | string | no | The `status.session.wokeAt` of the last wake that the `Display`'s node workload started. The node workload writes this field before its first command, so after a restart it sends nothing more for that wake. The `WakeApplied` condition reports the result. |
| <span id="status--standbyat"></span>`standbyAt` | string | no | The `status.session.standbyAt` of the last standby that the `Display`'s node workload started. The node workload writes this field before its first command, so after a restart it sends nothing more for that standby. The `StandbyApplied` condition reports the result. |
| <span id="status--screenask"></span>`screenAsk` | [object](#statusscreenask) | no | The last request for the `Player`'s screen that the `Display`'s adapter received on the bus. Its node workload writes the field under its own field manager. `media-operator` watches the `Television` objects and passes each new request once to the `Player`'s screen. It ignores a request that is already here when it starts, because that request is older than the start. `Wake` means that the TV broadcast Set Stream Path for the `Display` while the session was not awake, which a TV sends when a person picks the input in its source menu. `Sleep` means that the room received a Standby while the session was awake, either broadcast by any device or sent to the adapter by the TV, which a TV sends when a person turns it off. HDMI-CEC 1.3a, CEC 13.3.2, allows a playback device to ignore Standby. `liken` acts on it, so the `Player`'s screen goes dark with the TV. The screen sleeps only when nothing is playing. |
| <span id="status--powerread"></span>`powerRead` | [object](#statuspowerread) | no | The result of the last `status.session.powerReadAt`. The command adapter's node workload writes it under its own field manager, after it sends one Give Device Power Status to the TV. |
| <span id="status--displays"></span>`displays` | [\[\]object](#statusdisplays) | no | The `Display` objects whose picture reaches this TV, sorted by physical address. While the bus is in `Control`, the operator lists each `Display` that an adapter of the `CECBus` names in `spec.adapters[].display` and that has a physical address from its EDID. That adapter announces the `Display`'s physical address on this bus, which places the picture in this HDMI tree. A `Display` that no adapter names is not listed, even on a machine with an adapter of the bus, because the machine's other outputs can go to another TV, and a physical address does not say which tree it belongs to. |
| <span id="status--conditions"></span>`conditions` | [\[\]object](#statusconditions) | no | `Reachable`: whether the TV answers Give Device Power Status on its `CECBus`. It is `True` with the reason `Answers` when it does. It is `Unknown` with `Listening` while the bus is in `Listen`, with `NotScanned` until the bus finishes a scan, and with `Stale` when an adapter's entry is out of date. It is `False` with `NoBus` when the `CECBus` does not exist, with `NotFound` when no adapter finds a TV, with `Stopped` when the node workload stopped and released the adapter, and with `NoPowerStatus` when the TV acknowledges logical address 0 and does not answer. `InCharge`: whether this `Television` represents the TV of its bus. When several `Television` objects name one bus, one that a person declared comes before the discovered one, and within each group the first by name comes first. The one in charge is `True` with the reason `InCharge`. Each other one is `False` with `AnotherInCharge`, and its message names the one in charge. `PowerApplied`: whether the TV reported the state that `spec.power` asked for. It is `True` with the reason `Confirmed` when the TV did, `False` with `Unconfirmed` when it did not, and `False` with `Refused` when the adapter could not send. The message gives the command that the node workload sent, how many times it sent it, and the power that the TV last reported. `WakeApplied`: the result of the last wake in `status.session`. The `Display`'s node workload runs a wake only when the new `wokeAt` arrives while it runs. When `wokeAt` is already in `status.session` as the node workload starts, it sends nothing and logs that. A wake waits until `status.powerGeneration` matches the current generation of `spec.power`, and a new generation during a wake stops the wake, because a person's edit is newer than the wake. Before its first command, the node workload copies `wokeAt` to `status.wokeAt` and sets this condition to `Unknown` with the reason `Waking`. The wake turns the TV on as `spec.power` does, and claims the input with Image View On and Active Source for the `Display`'s physical address. For 30 seconds after the claim, the adapter claims the input again when another source takes it, and a person's choice of input ends that guard. [Wake the TV with the room](/docs/guides/connect-a-cec-adapter/#wake-the-tv-with-the-room) describes the steps and the guard. When the guard ends, the adapter reads the TV's power again. `WakeApplied` is `True` with the reason `Confirmed` when the TV reported `On` as it woke and again at the end of the guard, and the last Active Source on the bus is the session's `Display`. It is `False` with `Unconfirmed` when the TV did not report `On`, with `SourceTaken` when another source has the input at the end of the guard, with `Chosen` when a person's choice ended the guard, and with `Refused` when the adapter could not send. `Stopped` means that the session went to sleep, the bus changed, or the node workload stopped during the wake. `Superseded` means that a new generation of `spec.power` or another adapter's Active Source ended the wake. `TooLate` means that the wake had not started 2 minutes after the node workload first saw it, so the node workload sent nothing, because the room can have gone dark since. `SystemAudioApplied`: the result of the System Audio Mode Request of the last wake. When the session's `Display` has a `via` in `status.displays`, the wake asks that receiver for System Audio Mode, so the TV mutes its own speakers and passes its remote's volume keys to the receiver (HDMI-CEC 1.3a, CEC 13.15.2). The request carries the `Display`'s physical address, so it also switches the receiver to the `Display`'s input, and it can wake the receiver. The `Display`'s adapter sends the request once for each `wokeAt`, after the guard ends, and only when the last Active Source on the bus is the `Display`'s. So the request never takes the input from a person or from a source that the guard left alone. After the request, it waits 5 seconds for the receiver to broadcast Set System Audio Mode On, and ignores an On that arrived before the request. When none arrives, it sends Give System Audio Mode Status once, because the receiver sends its first On to the TV alone. The condition is `True` with the reason `Confirmed` for a broadcast On after the request or a status of On. It is `False` with `Unconfirmed` for a status of Off or no answer, which can mean that the receiver has HDMI control turned off or that the TV does not support the mode. It is `False` with `Refused` when the receiver answered with Feature Abort or the adapter could not send. The condition is absent after a wake that sent no request. `StandbyApplied`: the result of the last standby in `status.session`. The `Display`'s node workload runs a standby by the same rules as a wake: only for a new `standbyAt` that arrives while it runs, and only after `spec.power` is applied. Before its first command, the node workload copies `standbyAt` to `status.standbyAt` and sets this condition to `Unknown` with the reason `EnteringStandby`. It then puts the TV in standby as `spec.power` does: it reads the TV's power first, sends nothing when the TV already reports `Standby`, sends Standby to the TV alone, and sends at most three commands. The condition is `True` with the reason `Confirmed` when the TV reported `Standby`. It is `False` with `Unconfirmed` when the TV did not, and with `Refused` when the adapter could not send. `Stopped` means that a later wake, a change of the bus, or a stop of the node workload ended the standby. `Superseded` means that a new generation of `spec.power` ended it. `TooLate` means that the standby had not started 2 minutes after the node workload first saw it, so the node workload sent nothing. |

### status.cec

The TV's CEC identity, copied from the TV's entry in the `CECBus`'s `status.devices`. A field is absent until the TV reports it, and some TVs never report every field. For example, a TV can answer power status requests in standby and never answer Give OSD Name.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="statuscec--physicaladdress"></span>`physicalAddress` | string | no | The TV's physical address, always `0.0.0.0`. |
| <span id="statuscec--logicaladdress"></span>`logicalAddress` | integer | yes | The TV's logical address, always `0`. |
| <span id="statuscec--osdname"></span>`osdName` | string | no | The name that the TV reports, at most 14 characters. |
| <span id="statuscec--vendor"></span>`vendor` | string | no | The TV's IEEE OUI from its Device Vendor ID, as six hex digits. A Device Vendor ID of `000000` means no vendor, so the operator ignores it. The field keeps the last real vendor, or stays absent until the TV reports one. |
| <span id="statuscec--cecversion"></span>`cecVersion` | string | no | The CEC version that the TV reports, from `1.1` to `2.0`. |

### status.session

The `Receiver` session whose input shows on this TV, so that the TV wakes and goes to standby with the `Player`. The operator's `Deployment` writes it under its own field manager. So your apply of the spec does not remove it, and a write of it does not change `metadata.generation` or apply `spec.power` again. The operator takes the `Display` that is the monitor of the session's input in the `Receiver`'s `spec.inputs`, and writes the session to the `Television` whose `status.displays` lists that `Display`. It writes a new `wokeAt` when it sees the room wake: a `Play` starts on an existing session, the `Player`'s screen wakes, a `powerAsk` turns the room on, or a session appears with its `Play` or its screen already on. It writes a new `standbyAt` only when a `powerAsk` turns the room off. The `Display`'s adapter then wakes the TV and makes the `Display` the active source, or puts the TV in standby. When the operator starts, it keeps each session that it finds here with the same `Player` and `Display`, with its `awake`, `wokeAt`, and `standbyAt` unchanged, and it wakes nothing and puts nothing in standby. The operator removes the field 60 seconds after the `Receiver`'s session ends, the `Receiver` is deleted, or the `Receiver`'s address changes, unless a session of the same `Player` starts first. So when `media-operator` removes a session and writes it again a moment later, the TV is not woken again. If the API server refuses the removal, the operator tries again after 10 seconds.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="statussession--player"></span>`player` | string | yes | The `Player` that owns the `Receiver` session, as `namespace/name`. |
| <span id="statussession--display"></span>`display` | string | yes | The `Display` that is the monitor of the session's input in the `Receiver`'s `spec.inputs`. |
| <span id="statussession--awake"></span>`awake` | boolean | no | `true` while the session keeps the room on: from a wake until a `powerAsk` on the `Receiver` turns the room off, or until the `Play` and the `Player`'s screen are both off. While it is `true`, the `Display`'s adapter reports its own power to the TV as `On`. It answers a Request Active Source, and a Set Stream Path for the `Display`'s physical address, with Active Source for the `Display`, until the route moves away from the `Display`. The answer has no Image View On before it, so it cannot wake a TV that a person turned off. When it changes to `false`, a wake in progress stops. It does not put the TV in standby. Only a new `standbyAt` does that. With no new `standbyAt`, the adapter sends the TV Inactive Source if the route still leads to the `Display` (HDMI-CEC 1.3a, CEC 13.2.2). While it is `false`, the adapter reports `Standby`, because a playback device with no picture is in standby, and it sends no Active Source. A Set Stream Path for the `Display` then asks the `Player`'s screen to wake through `status.screenAsk`, and the adapter reports In transition Standby to On until the screen wakes. [Wake the TV with the room](/docs/guides/connect-a-cec-adapter/#wake-the-tv-with-the-room) describes the answers and the wake. |
| <span id="statussession--wokeat"></span>`wokeAt` | string | no | When the operator saw the session wake the room, in RFC 3339 with milliseconds. Each new value is a new wake, so a `powerAsk` can wake the room again while `awake` is already `true`. The node workload compares the value only to tell one wake from another, and measures the wake's age on its own clock. |
| <span id="statussession--standbyat"></span>`standbyAt` | string | no | When a `status.session.powerAsk` on the `Receiver` turned the room off, in RFC 3339 with milliseconds. Each new value is one standby. The operator writes it only for a `powerAsk` that turns a room off while the room is on. `media-operator` writes a `powerAsk` of `off` when the `Player`'s `spec.power` changes to `Off`, from the power key or from an edit with `kubectl`. The room is on when the TV reports `On` or `ToOn`. When the room has no `Television` or the TV does not report its power, the receiver's power decides. A `Play` that ends, a screen that sleeps, a session that ends, and an operator restart write no `standbyAt`, because a TV often shows another input, such as a streaming player, while the `Player` is idle. The same write sets `awake` to `false`, and a later wake removes this field. The node workload compares the value only to tell one standby from another, and measures the standby's age on its own clock. |
| <span id="statussession--powerreadat"></span>`powerReadAt` | string | no | When a `status.session.powerAsk` on the `Receiver` asked for a fresh read of the TV's power, in RFC 3339 with milliseconds. Each new value is one request. `status.power` can be out of date, because a person can turn the TV on or off with its own remote, and the TV can send nothing that the adapters receive. The operator writes a new value for each `powerAsk` when an adapter in `Control` has found the TV and this `Television`'s session belongs to the `Player` whose `Receiver` session has the `powerAsk`. This includes a TV that is not `Reachable` with the reason `NoPowerStatus`, because such a TV can still be on. The operator then waits up to 3 seconds for the result in `status.powerRead`. It uses that result to decide whether the room is on, or uses `status.power` when no result arrives. The command adapter's node workload reads the TV's power once for each new value. It ignores a value that is already here when it starts, because that value is older than the 3-second wait. Any other write of the session removes the field. |
| <span id="statussession--showat"></span>`showAt` | string | no | When a press of a controller's home key asked the TV to show the session's `Display`, in RFC 3339 with milliseconds. Each new value is one request. A TV that shows its own apps is on another input, so switching the receiver's input alone does not bring the `Player` back. For a home press, `media-operator` writes a show request in the `Receiver`'s `status.session.inputAsk`. The operator then writes a new value here when this session belongs to the `Player` of the press, is for the same `Display`, and is awake. It writes nothing for a session that is not awake, because a home press does not wake a room that is off. The `Display`'s adapter then sends Image View On and Active Source for the `Display`. It sends Image View On even to a TV that reports `On`, because a TV that shows an internal app switches input on that pair, which is the sequence of One Touch Play, and not on Active Source alone. It reads no power first, because the session's `Player` is on. It sends nothing during a wake, because the wake switches the input itself. It ignores a value that is already here when the node workload starts, because that value is older than the press. Any other write of the session removes the field. |

### status.screenAsk

The last request for the `Player`'s screen that the `Display`'s adapter received on the bus. Its node workload writes the field under its own field manager. `media-operator` watches the `Television` objects and passes each new request once to the `Player`'s screen. It ignores a request that is already here when it starts, because that request is older than the start. `Wake` means that the TV broadcast Set Stream Path for the `Display` while the session was not awake, which a TV sends when a person picks the input in its source menu. `Sleep` means that the room received a Standby while the session was awake, either broadcast by any device or sent to the adapter by the TV, which a TV sends when a person turns it off. HDMI-CEC 1.3a, CEC 13.3.2, allows a playback device to ignore Standby. `liken` acts on it, so the `Player`'s screen goes dark with the TV. The screen sleeps only when nothing is playing.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="statusscreenask--at"></span>`at` | string | yes | When the node workload received the message, in RFC 3339 with milliseconds. Each new value is one request. |
| <span id="statusscreenask--player"></span>`player` | string | yes | The `Player` whose screen the request is for, as `namespace/name`. |
| <span id="statusscreenask--screen"></span>`screen` | string | yes | What the request asks the screen to do: `Wake` or `Sleep`. One of: `Wake`, `Sleep`. |
| <span id="statusscreenask--cause"></span>`cause` | string | no | A description of the bus message, which `media-operator` writes in its log line when it passes the request on. |

### status.powerRead

The result of the last `status.session.powerReadAt`. The command adapter's node workload writes it under its own field manager, after it sends one Give Device Power Status to the TV.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="statuspowerread--at"></span>`at` | string | yes | The `status.session.powerReadAt` that this read is for. |
| <span id="statuspowerread--power"></span>`power` | string | no | The power status that the TV reported: `On`, `Standby`, `ToOn`, or `ToStandby`. It is absent when the TV did not answer. |

### status.displays[]

The `Display` objects whose picture reaches this TV, sorted by physical address. While the bus is in `Control`, the operator lists each `Display` that an adapter of the `CECBus` names in `spec.adapters[].display` and that has a physical address from its EDID. That adapter announces the `Display`'s physical address on this bus, which places the picture in this HDMI tree. A `Display` that no adapter names is not listed, even on a machine with an adapter of the bus, because the machine's other outputs can go to another TV, and a physical address does not say which tree it belongs to.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="statusdisplays--name"></span>`name` | string | yes | The name of the `Display`. |
| <span id="statusdisplays--physicaladdress"></span>`physicalAddress` | string | yes | The `Display`'s physical address from `display-operator`, in dotted form such as `1.3.0.0`. |
| <span id="statusdisplays--via"></span>`via` | [object](#statusdisplaysvia) | no | The `Receiver` that the picture passes through on its way to the TV. The operator sets it when the `CECBus` has an audio system whose physical address is above the `Display`'s, and a `Receiver` has an input whose machine is the `Display`'s machine and whose monitor is this `Display`. When several `Receiver` objects match, it takes the first by name. For example, an audio system at `1.0.0.0` is above a `Display` at `1.3.0.0` and not above one at `2.0.0.0`. The field is absent when no audio system is on the path, for example when a `Receiver`'s optical input carries the sound of a `Display` that connects straight to the TV. A wake asks this receiver for System Audio Mode. |

#### status.displays[].via

The `Receiver` that the picture passes through on its way to the TV. The operator sets it when the `CECBus` has an audio system whose physical address is above the `Display`'s, and a `Receiver` has an input whose machine is the `Display`'s machine and whose monitor is this `Display`. When several `Receiver` objects match, it takes the first by name. For example, an audio system at `1.0.0.0` is above a `Display` at `1.3.0.0` and not above one at `2.0.0.0`. The field is absent when no audio system is on the path, for example when a `Receiver`'s optical input carries the sound of a `Display` that connects straight to the TV. A wake asks this receiver for System Audio Mode.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

### status.conditions[]

`Reachable`: whether the TV answers Give Device Power Status on its `CECBus`. It is `True` with the reason `Answers` when it does. It is `Unknown` with `Listening` while the bus is in `Listen`, with `NotScanned` until the bus finishes a scan, and with `Stale` when an adapter's entry is out of date. It is `False` with `NoBus` when the `CECBus` does not exist, with `NotFound` when no adapter finds a TV, with `Stopped` when the node workload stopped and released the adapter, and with `NoPowerStatus` when the TV acknowledges logical address 0 and does not answer. `InCharge`: whether this `Television` represents the TV of its bus. When several `Television` objects name one bus, one that a person declared comes before the discovered one, and within each group the first by name comes first. The one in charge is `True` with the reason `InCharge`. Each other one is `False` with `AnotherInCharge`, and its message names the one in charge. `PowerApplied`: whether the TV reported the state that `spec.power` asked for. It is `True` with the reason `Confirmed` when the TV did, `False` with `Unconfirmed` when it did not, and `False` with `Refused` when the adapter could not send. The message gives the command that the node workload sent, how many times it sent it, and the power that the TV last reported. `WakeApplied`: the result of the last wake in `status.session`. The `Display`'s node workload runs a wake only when the new `wokeAt` arrives while it runs. When `wokeAt` is already in `status.session` as the node workload starts, it sends nothing and logs that. A wake waits until `status.powerGeneration` matches the current generation of `spec.power`, and a new generation during a wake stops the wake, because a person's edit is newer than the wake. Before its first command, the node workload copies `wokeAt` to `status.wokeAt` and sets this condition to `Unknown` with the reason `Waking`. The wake turns the TV on as `spec.power` does, and claims the input with Image View On and Active Source for the `Display`'s physical address. For 30 seconds after the claim, the adapter claims the input again when another source takes it, and a person's choice of input ends that guard. [Wake the TV with the room](/docs/guides/connect-a-cec-adapter/#wake-the-tv-with-the-room) describes the steps and the guard. When the guard ends, the adapter reads the TV's power again. `WakeApplied` is `True` with the reason `Confirmed` when the TV reported `On` as it woke and again at the end of the guard, and the last Active Source on the bus is the session's `Display`. It is `False` with `Unconfirmed` when the TV did not report `On`, with `SourceTaken` when another source has the input at the end of the guard, with `Chosen` when a person's choice ended the guard, and with `Refused` when the adapter could not send. `Stopped` means that the session went to sleep, the bus changed, or the node workload stopped during the wake. `Superseded` means that a new generation of `spec.power` or another adapter's Active Source ended the wake. `TooLate` means that the wake had not started 2 minutes after the node workload first saw it, so the node workload sent nothing, because the room can have gone dark since. `SystemAudioApplied`: the result of the System Audio Mode Request of the last wake. When the session's `Display` has a `via` in `status.displays`, the wake asks that receiver for System Audio Mode, so the TV mutes its own speakers and passes its remote's volume keys to the receiver (HDMI-CEC 1.3a, CEC 13.15.2). The request carries the `Display`'s physical address, so it also switches the receiver to the `Display`'s input, and it can wake the receiver. The `Display`'s adapter sends the request once for each `wokeAt`, after the guard ends, and only when the last Active Source on the bus is the `Display`'s. So the request never takes the input from a person or from a source that the guard left alone. After the request, it waits 5 seconds for the receiver to broadcast Set System Audio Mode On, and ignores an On that arrived before the request. When none arrives, it sends Give System Audio Mode Status once, because the receiver sends its first On to the TV alone. The condition is `True` with the reason `Confirmed` for a broadcast On after the request or a status of On. It is `False` with `Unconfirmed` for a status of Off or no answer, which can mean that the receiver has HDMI control turned off or that the TV does not support the mode. It is `False` with `Refused` when the receiver answered with Feature Abort or the adapter could not send. The condition is absent after a wake that sent no request. `StandbyApplied`: the result of the last standby in `status.session`. The `Display`'s node workload runs a standby by the same rules as a wake: only for a new `standbyAt` that arrives while it runs, and only after `spec.power` is applied. Before its first command, the node workload copies `standbyAt` to `status.standbyAt` and sets this condition to `Unknown` with the reason `EnteringStandby`. It then puts the TV in standby as `spec.power` does: it reads the TV's power first, sends nothing when the TV already reports `Standby`, sends Standby to the TV alone, and sends at most three commands. The condition is `True` with the reason `Confirmed` when the TV reported `Standby`. It is `False` with `Unconfirmed` when the TV did not, and with `Refused` when the adapter could not send. `Stopped` means that a later wake, a change of the bus, or a stop of the node workload ended the standby. `Superseded` means that a new generation of `spec.power` ended it. `TooLate` means that the standby had not started 2 minutes after the node workload first saw it, so the node workload sent nothing.
